text: In October 1986 the LBL-Berkeley link fell from 32 kb/s to 40 b/s. What happened?
choices: Congestion collapse: queues filled, senders retransmitted, retransmissions added load, and the fraction of capacity carrying useful data collapsed
explanation: The critical property is that it is stable — it does not recover when load decreases, because the retransmissions sustain it. The original TCP had no defence because its designers had not distinguished overwhelming a receiver from overwhelming the network.
